_note: Frozen content for design review. Highlight family — a full-bleed band holding the statement, with solid marks on the words that carry the argument, and three facts underneath.
brief: Six things that make software expensive, none of which are the code

slots.titleLine1: Writing it was never the expensive part
slots.subtitle: Six costs that appear on no estimate and account for most of what a project consumes.

slots.statementLine1: A change waiting for review is not idle, it is
slots.fact1Body: Against four hours of actual work in the change itself.
slots.fact2Body: Context leaves the author's head within a day and has to be rebuilt.
slots.fact3Body: Not because people work faster, but because the queue stops compounding.

slots.statementLine1: Most rework is not a quality failure, it is
slots.fact1Body: The largest single line, and the cheapest one to remove.
slots.fact2Body: Difficulty is real and it is nearly the smallest part of the bill.
slots.fact3Body: Consistently outperforms a week of careful implementation.

slots.statementLine1: Coordination scales with headcount, and it scales
slots.fact1Body: Against four and a half hours of uninterrupted work in the same week.
slots.fact2Body: Almost all of it spent rebuilding the context, not answering.
slots.fact3Body: Adding one person to a team of six adds six new lines of communication.

slots.statementLine1: A decision with no owner does not get made, it gets
slots.fact1Body: Measured from the question being asked to anything happening.
slots.fact2Body: The same decision, the same information, one person accountable.
slots.fact3Body: That is the price of speed, and it was worth seven days every time.

slots.statementLine1: Teams re-argue settled decisions because nobody recorded
slots.fact1Body: Written the day it was made, or it does not get written at all.
slots.fact2Body: How often an undocumented decision comes back for another round.
slots.fact3Body: Which is why it is the one nobody can justify skipping afterwards.

slots.titleLine1: None of it is a tools problem
slots.statementLine1: Every team with a perfect stack still ships slowly if
slots.fact1Body: Five migrations, no change in how long anything took.
slots.fact2Body: One owner per decision, applied without exception for a quarter.
slots.fact3Body: Which is unfortunate, because process is harder to buy than software.

slots.ctaLine1: Count the waiting before you cut anything
slots.statementLine1: The cheapest hour you will ever spend is the one that
slots.ctaBody: Not the tooling, not the headcount, and not the code review standard. Measure elapsed time from ready to done, and the answer names itself.
slots.signoff: Everything else is guessing with conviction
